intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters ideal for beginner snorkelers. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit
experiences.description: Spend a full day immersing the family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures including Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Tahitian, and Maori. Enjoy live demonstrations, canoe rides, traditional crafts, and an incredible evening luau with fire knife dancing and an all-you-can-eat buffet. One of the most educational and entertaining family experiences on the islands.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a leisurely day on one of America's most celebrated beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand on Maui's west coast. Families can swim in calm turquoise waters, build sandcastles, rent boogie boards, and watch cliff divers leap from Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) at sunset. Beachside restaurants and shave ice stands make it a perfect all-day outing.

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. The park's visitor center offers ranger-led programs designed specifically for children, making it both thrilling and educational.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

experiences.name: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food by visiting iconic local spots serving plate lunches featuring kalua pork, lomi salmon, poi, macaroni salad, and fresh poke bowls. Stop at legendary local institutions like Helena's Hawaiian Food and grab shave ice from Matsumoto's for dessert. A delicious and affordable way to connect the whole family with Hawaii's unique culinary heritage.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration

Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hawaii airport at 11:20 AM — collect luggage, pick up a lei greeting at the terminal, and arrange ground transportation to your accommodation. Take time to freshen up and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby local beach for a relaxed first afternoon. Waimea Bay or Ala Moana Beach Park (depending on your island base) offers free entry, calm waters, and beautiful scenery perfect for families. Rent a beach mat from a local vendor (~$5) and soak in the Hawaiian sun.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the waterfront promenade and watch the sunset. Visit a nearby ABC Store for affordable snacks and essentials. Explore the local neighborhood to get your bearings.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at the airport — look for local plate lunch counters or a convenience store for a budget-friendly snack (~$8-10)
meals.lunch: Pick up a classic Hawaiian plate lunch from a local food truck near the beach — try spam musubi, macaroni salad, and rice (~$10-12)
meals.dinner: Visit a local grocery store like Foodland or Times Supermarket for a budget dinner — grab poke bowls from the deli counter, a Hawaiian staple at great value (~$12-15)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the late morning arrival. Focus on settling in, hydrating, and adjusting to the time zone. Pack reef-safe sunscreen — it's required in Hawaii and can be expensive to buy locally. August weather averages around 16.8°C with some rain, so pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve (arrive early — gates open at 6:45 AM and it fills up fast). This world-famous snorkeling spot is ideal for families. Entry fee is $25 per adult, free for children under 13. Rent snorkel gear on-site (~$12) and explore the vibrant coral reef teeming with tropical fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive along the scenic Kalanianaole Highway to Makapu'u Point Lighthouse Trail — a free, paved 2-mile round-trip hike with stunning ocean views and whale-watching potential. Great for kids and budget-friendly.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Kailua Town for a relaxed evening walk. Browse local shops and enjoy the charming small-town Hawaiian atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast at the hotel or grab fresh fruit and yogurt from a local grocery store (~$5-7)
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from the grocery store to enjoy at Makapu'u Point — saves money and is convenient for families (~$8-10 total)
meals.dinner: Try Kalapawai Market in Kailua for affordable sandwiches, salads, and local comfort food in a casual setting (~$12-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Hanauma Bay reservations online in advance — they sell out quickly, especially in August. Bring water shoes for the rocky reef entry. The lighthouse trail is stroller-friendly for younger children.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Diamond Head State Monument — one of Hawaii's most iconic landmarks. The 1.6-mile round-trip hike to the crater summit offers panoramic views of Honolulu and Waikiki. Entry is $5 per person. Start early (opens at 6 AM) to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Waikiki Beach — Hawaii's most famous stretch of sand. Enjoy free beach time, build sandcastles with the kids, and watch outrigger canoe paddlers. Rent a bodyboard from a beach vendor (~$10/hour) for extra fun.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Kalakaua Avenue in Waikiki to enjoy free street entertainment, hula dancers, and the lively atmosphere. Watch the free torch lighting and hula ceremony at the Kuhio Beach Hula Mound (held nightly at sunset).

meals.breakfast: Visit Leonard's Bakery for their famous malasadas (Portuguese donuts) — a beloved local treat at about $1.50 each (~$8-10 for the family)
meals.lunch: Grab shave ice at Matsumoto's or a local shave ice stand near Waikiki (~$4-6 each) plus a plate lunch from a food truck (~$10-12)
meals.dinner: Try Ono Seafood in Honolulu for affordable, fresh poke bowls — a local favorite with generous portions (~$12-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head can get very hot by mid-morning — start as early as possible and bring plenty of water. The free hula show at Kuhio Beach is a wonderful cultural experience for the whole family and runs Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Polynesian Cultural Center (PCC) — book in advance for the best rates. The daytime village experience lets families explore six authentic Polynesian villages (Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Tahitian, and Māori). Budget tickets start around $60-70 per adult, $50 for children — look for online discount codes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the PCC villages and participate in hands-on cultural activities like coconut husking, fire-making, and traditional weaving. These interactive experiences are fantastic for kids and deeply educational.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Ha: Breath of Life evening show at PCC — an incredible Polynesian performance included with most ticket packages. A truly memorable family experience.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel or prepare a simple meal before heading out — the PCC is about an hour's drive from Honolulu (~$5-8)
meals.lunch: Dine at the Gateway Restaurant inside PCC — the all-you-can-eat buffet with Hawaiian and Polynesian dishes is included in some ticket packages or available for ~$20-25 per person
meals.dinner: Dinner is included with the evening show package at PCC, or grab affordable plate lunches from food stands within the center (~$12-15)

day_by_day.notes: The Polynesian Cultural Center is located on the North Shore in Laie — plan for a full day trip. Purchase tickets online in advance for the best prices and to guarantee availability. This is one of the best family-friendly cultural experiences in Hawaii and well worth the splurge.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the North Shore of Oahu — drive to Haleiwa Town, a charming surf village with colorful shops and galleries. Walk the historic town, visit the Haleiwa Farmers Market (if running), and browse local art. Completely free to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waimea Bay Beach Park for an afternoon of swimming and cliff jumping (for older kids and adults — the famous rock jump is about 25 feet). The bay is calm in summer, making it ideal for families. Free entry.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back along the scenic Kamehameha Highway, stopping at Sunset Beach for a breathtaking evening view. The North Shore sunsets are legendary.

meals.breakfast: Stop at Matsumoto Shave Ice in Haleiwa for their famous shave ice and a light breakfast snack (~$8-10)
meals.lunch: Try Giovanni's Shrimp Truck — a North Shore institution. The garlic shrimp plate is legendary and very affordable (~$14-16 per plate, easily shared)
meals.dinner: Pick up groceries at a local store on the way back and prepare a simple dinner at the hotel, or grab affordable takeout from a local diner (~$10-12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore is about 45-60 minutes from Honolulu. August is summer in Hawaii, so ocean conditions at Waimea Bay are generally calm and safe for swimming — the massive winter waves are not present. Always check ocean conditions before swimming. Giovanni's Shrimp Truck often has a line — arrive early or be prepared to wait.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial — a deeply moving and historically significant site. The USS Arizona Memorial is free (boat shuttle tickets are timed and must be reserved online in advance at recreation.gov). Arrive early as tickets go fast. The visitor center and exhibits are free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the additional Pearl Harbor attractions — the Battleship Missouri Memorial ($32 adult, $16 children) or the Pacific Aviation Museum ($25 adult, $15 children) offer fascinating insights into WWII history. Choose one based on your family's interests and budget.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Honolulu and visit Chinatown for an evening stroll. Explore the colorful markets, art galleries, and cultural landmarks in this historic neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel before heading out — Pearl Harbor is best visited on an empty stomach as food options inside are limited and pricey (~$5-8 at hotel)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the Pearl Harbor visitor center café or pack your own lunch to eat in the picnic area (~$10-12)
meals.dinner: Explore Chinatown's affordable dining scene — try Little Village Noodle House for delicious Chinese-Hawaiian fusion at budget-friendly prices (~$12-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor is one of the most visited sites in Hawaii — book USS Arizona Memorial boat tickets weeks in advance as they are free but extremely limited. No bags larger than a small purse are allowed inside the memorial. This is a solemn site — remind children to be respectful. The experience is deeply educational for older children.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Big Island to visit Hawaii Volcanoes National Park — one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes. Fly inter-island (budget ~$80-120 round trip per person on Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest) or join an affordable group tour. The park entrance fee is $35 per vehicle (valid for 7 days).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the park's highlights — walk the Kilauea Iki Trail (4-mile loop through a hardened lava lake), visit the Thurston Lava Tube (a magical walk through an ancient lava tunnel), and drive the Chain of Craters Road for dramatic coastal lava views. Check the park website for current volcanic activity updates.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Jaggar Museum overlook (or Kilauea Overlook) at dusk for a spectacular view of the glowing lava lake in Halema'uma'u Crater — one of Hawaii's most awe-inspiring natural spectacles. Return to Oahu on an evening flight.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel before your early morning flight to the Big Island (~$5-8)
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks for the park — food options inside Hawaii Volcanoes National Park are limited. The Volcano House restaurant is available but pricier (~$8-10 packed lunch)
meals.dinner: Grab a quick meal at Hilo Airport before your return flight, or eat upon return to Oahu at a local food truck (~$12-15)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long day — start very early to maximize time at the park. Book inter-island flights well in advance for the best prices. Check the National Park Service website (nps.gov/havo) for current volcanic activity and trail conditions before visiting. Volcanic fumes (vog) can be an issue — those with respiratory conditions should take precautions. Bring layers as the park sits at elevation and can be cool and rainy.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bishop Museum — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. Admission is $25 for adults, $17 for children (ages 4-17). Explore the Hawaiian Hall, planetarium shows, and fascinating exhibits on Pacific Island cultures, natural history, and Hawaiian royalty. A wonderful educational experience for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ala Moana Beach Park — a beautiful, free public beach adjacent to the famous Ala Moana Shopping Center. Enjoy swimming, picnicking, and relaxing on the wide sandy beach. The park has excellent facilities including restrooms, showers, and picnic tables.
day_by_day.evening: Browse Ala Moana Center — Hawaii's largest open-air shopping mall. Window shop, enjoy free entertainment, and pick up affordable souvenirs from stores like Longs Drugs or ABC Stores. Watch the free hula show performed at the mall's Centerstage (check schedule online).

meals.breakfast: Visit a local diner or café near the hotel for a hearty breakfast — look for local spots serving loco moco (rice, hamburger patty, egg, and gravy) — a filling Hawaiian classic (~$10-12)
meals.lunch: Enjoy a picnic lunch at Ala Moana Beach Park — pick up supplies from the nearby Foodland grocery store for a budget-friendly spread (~$8-10 per person)
meals.dinner: Visit the Ala Moana Center Food Court for affordable and diverse dining options — try Panda Express, Goma Tei Ramen, or local Hawaiian plate lunch counters (~$10-14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Bishop Museum is a fantastic rainy day option — August can bring afternoon showers, so having an indoor activity planned is smart. Check the museum's website for any special exhibits or planetarium show schedules. Ala Moana Beach Park is one of Oahu's best family beaches with calm, protected waters ideal for young swimmers.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Manoa Falls Trail — a beautiful, lush rainforest hike leading to a stunning 150-foot waterfall. The trail is 1.6 miles round trip and suitable for families with older children. Parking is $5, and the trail itself is free. Wear waterproof shoes as the trail can be muddy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Lyon Arboretum adjacent to the trailhead — a free botanical garden with over 5,000 tropical plant species spread across 194 acres. A peaceful and educational afternoon exploring Hawaii's incredible plant diversity.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Kaimana Beach (Sans Souci Beach) near Diamond Head for a relaxed evening swim and sunset viewing. This quieter alternative to Waikiki is beloved by locals and offers a more authentic Hawaiian beach experience.

meals.breakfast: Stop at a local bakery or café in Manoa Valley for fresh pastries and coffee before the hike (~$8-10)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy at the arboretum or after the hike — pick up supplies from a nearby grocery store (~$8-10 per person)
meals.dinner: Try Rainbow Drive-In near Kapahulu Avenue — a beloved local institution serving affordable plate lunches and Hawaiian comfort food since 1961 (~$10-12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Manoa Falls Trail passes through a genuine Hawaiian rainforest — mosquito repellent is strongly recommended. The trail can be slippery after rain (very common in Manoa Valley), so waterproof footwear is essential. Do not swim in the pool at the base of the falls due to leptospirosis risk from the water. Lyon Arboretum requires a small donation or reservation — check their website in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Spend your final morning at Lanikai Beach — consistently rated one of the most beautiful beaches in the world. The powdery white sand and crystal-clear turquoise water are absolutely stunning. Completely free to visit. Take a final swim, collect shells, and soak in the paradise one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at local markets or ABC Stores. Visit the Kailua Farmers Market (if available) for unique local products, Hawaiian honey, macadamia nuts, and handmade crafts at reasonable prices. Pack your bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport for your departure flight. Arrive at least 2-3 hours early for international/mainland flights. Reflect on an incredible 10 days in paradise.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a final Hawaiian breakfast at Boots & Kimo's Homestyle Kitchen in Kailua — famous for their macadamia nut pancakes. A beloved local spot worth the splurge on your last day (~$12-15 per person)
meals.lunch: Grab a final plate lunch from a local food truck or Kalapawai Market in Kailua — enjoy it as a picnic near the beach (~$10-12 per person)
meals.dinner: Eat at the airport or grab affordable takeout before your flight — look for local options in the terminal rather than chain restaurants (~$12-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Lanikai Beach has limited parking — arrive early or park in the Kailua Beach Park lot and walk over. Note that Hawaii has strict agricultural inspection rules — you cannot bring most fresh fruits, plants, or certain food items back to the mainland. Check USDA guidelines before packing. Consider buying vacuum-sealed macadamia nuts, Kona coffee, and Hawaiian sea salt as budget-friendly, TSA-approved souvenirs. Mahalo for an amazing trip!

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 11:20 AM — no morning activities scheduled. Upon landing, collect luggage, pick up rental car or arrange shuttle transfer to accommodation area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park. Freshen up and take a leisurely stroll around the Buena Park/Anaheim area to get oriented. Visit a nearby grocery or convenience store to stock up on snacks and essentials for the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Easy, low-key first evening — explore the Buena Park dining strip along Beach Boulevard. Window-shop and relax after the flight. Early bedtime to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or light meal at the airport before or after landing — try a local Hawaiian-style café in the terminal if available.
meals.lunch: Pick up a casual bite near the hotel — Raising Cane's or In-N-Out Burger on Beach Blvd for a quick, affordable post-travel meal (~$10–15/person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sizzler on Beach Blvd or nearby Denny's for a relaxed, family-friendly, budget-conscious meal (~$15–20/person).

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 11:20 AM arrival. Prioritize rest and settling in. Confirm any pre-booked Hawaii activity reservations and review the upcoming itinerary as a family.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Knott's Berry Farm (just 5 minutes from the hotel on Beach Blvd) — a classic Southern California theme park perfect for families. Arrive at opening (10 AM) to beat crowds. Enjoy rides like GhostRider and Snoopy-themed areas for younger kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Knott's Berry Farm through the afternoon. Try the iconic Boysenberry-themed food offerings throughout the park. Visit Camp Snoopy for family-friendly rides and photo opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the hotel to freshen up, then explore Downtown Disney or the Anaheim GardenWalk for evening entertainment and dining (10–15 min drive).

meals.breakfast: Hotel continental breakfast or grab pastries and coffee at a nearby Starbucks or Panera Bread before heading to the park.
meals.lunch: Lunch inside Knott's Berry Farm — try the famous Mrs. Knott's Chicken Dinner Restaurant for their signature fried chicken (~$20–25/person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bubba Gump Shrimp Co. at Anaheim GardenWalk for a fun, family-friendly seafood experience (~$20–30/person).

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Knott's Berry Farm tickets online in advance for discounts (typically $30–50/person vs. gate price). Check the park's website for any seasonal August events or shows.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Disneyland Park (15-minute drive from hotel). Arrive at rope drop (8–9 AM) to maximize time. Head straight to popular rides like Space Mountain, Pirates of the Caribbean, and Haunted Mansion before crowds build.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Disneyland — explore Fantasyland and Tomorrowland with the family. Catch a midday parade or character meet-and-greet. Take a midday break at the hotel if needed (especially with young children).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Disneyland for the evening to catch the spectacular Fantasmic! nighttime show and fireworks display over Sleeping Beauty Castle.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or grab a quick bite at a nearby McDonald's before park opening to save time.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Blue Bayou Restaurant inside Pirates of the Caribbean at Disneyland — a unique, atmospheric dining experience (reserve in advance, ~$30–40/person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Plaza Inn on Main Street, U.S.A. for classic fried chicken and comfort food (~$20–25/person) before the evening show.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Disneyland tickets well in advance — prices vary by date (typically $104–189/person). Consider the Genie+ add-on (~$25–35/person) to skip lines on popular attractions. Wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Disney California Adventure Park (adjacent to Disneyland). Start with Radiator Springs Racers in Cars Land and Guardians of the Galaxy – Mission: BREAKOUT! early before lines grow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy Pixar Pier with family-friendly rides including the Incredicoaster and Toy Story Midway Mania. Explore Avengers Campus for Marvel-themed experiences and character encounters.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for World of Color — a stunning nighttime water, light, and projection show at Paradise Bay. Great finale to the Disneyland Resort experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Flo's V8 Café in Cars Land for a themed, hearty start to the day (~$15–20/person).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Shawarma Palace in Avengers Campus for a fun Marvel-themed quick-service meal (~$15–18/person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Carthay Circle Restaurant — a mid-range sit-down option with California cuisine (~$30–45/person). Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Your Disneyland Resort ticket may cover both parks on the same day depending on the ticket type purchased. Verify your ticket type before this day. Arrive early to secure a good viewing spot for World of Color.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Huntington Beach (approx. 30 minutes from hotel) — known as 'Surf City USA.' Walk the famous Huntington Beach Pier, watch surfers, and enjoy the laid-back beach town atmosphere. Great warm-up beach day before Hawaii.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon relaxing on Huntington Beach — build sandcastles, swim in the Pacific, or rent bikes along the beachfront path. Visit the International Surfing Museum nearby for a fun, quick cultural stop.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Huntington Beach's Main Street for shopping, ice cream, and a casual dinner before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or stop at a local café en route — try Keke's Breakfast Café or IHOP near the hotel (~$10–15/person).
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Duke's Huntington Beach — a Hawaiian-themed restaurant right on the sand, perfect for getting into the Hawaii spirit (~$20–30/person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Wahoo's Fish Taco on Main Street, Huntington Beach — casual, fresh, and affordable (~$12–18/person).

day_by_day.notes: Free parking is available along Pacific Coast Highway (metered) or in city lots near the pier (~$2–3/hour). Bring sunscreen, towels, and beach gear. This is a great day to mentally transition into 'beach vacation mode' ahead of Hawaii.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of SureStay Hotel and head to LAX or John Wayne Airport (SNA) for your flight to Honolulu, Oahu. Allow ample time for check-in and security. Upon arrival in Honolulu, collect luggage and arrange ground transportation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your Honolulu accommodation (mid-range hotel near Waikiki recommended — e.g., Aston Waikiki Beach Hotel or similar, ~$150–200/night). Take a first walk along Waikiki Beach to soak in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Kalakaua Avenue — Waikiki's main strip. Browse ABC Stores for local snacks and souvenirs. Watch the sunset from the beach and enjoy a relaxed first evening in Hawaii.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or airport before departure — grab a quick meal at the terminal.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Honolulu airport or a quick stop near your hotel upon arrival — try Zippy's, a beloved local Hawaii chain (~$10–15/person).
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at Duke's Waikiki on the beach — a classic Honolulu institution with Hawaiian-inspired seafood and cocktails (~$25–40/person). Make a reservation.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your inter-island or mainland-to-Hawaii flight details in advance. Waikiki is the ideal base for Oahu exploration. Pick up a local SIM card or activate an international data plan upon arrival. Weather in August averages 16.8°C highs with some rain — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries. Arrive early (7–8 AM) as the bay has a daily visitor cap and fills up fast. Watch the mandatory marine education video, then snorkel among hundreds of colorful tropical fish in crystal-clear waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay, drive the scenic southeastern Oahu coastline — stop at Halona Blowhole Lookout and Sandy Beach Park for stunning views and photo opportunities. Continue to Makapu'u Point Lighthouse Trail for a short, rewarding family hike with panoramic ocean views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxed evening at Kuhio Beach — watch the free hula and torch lighting ceremony held nightly at sunset on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before Hanauma Bay — grab malasadas (Portuguese donuts) from Leonard's Bakery on Kapahulu Ave, a Hawaii institution (~$1–2 each).
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Hanauma Bay or grab plate lunches from a nearby food truck along Kalanianaole Highway (~$10–14/person).
meals.dinner: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour experience — visit iconic local spots like Rainbow Drive-In or Ono Hawaiian Foods in Kapahulu for authentic loco moco, kalua pork, and poi (~$12–18/person).

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay reservations are REQUIRED and must be booked online in advance at hawaiistateparks.org. Entry fee is $25/adult, free for Hawaii residents and children under 13. Bring reef-safe sunscreen only — chemical sunscreens are banned to protect the reef.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit — depart early from Waikiki (45-minute drive to Laie on the North Shore). Spend the morning exploring the six Polynesian village exhibits representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa (New Zealand), Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Participate in hands-on cultural activities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue at the Polynesian Cultural Center — watch live cultural demonstrations, canoe pageants on the lagoon, and interactive shows. The center is a full-day experience ideal for families with children of all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the spectacular 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show — a world-class Polynesian theatrical performance with fire dancing, drumming, and storytelling. Included with most ticket packages.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departing — or stop at Ted's Bakery on the North Shore (near Sunset Beach) en route for famous cream pies and local breakfast plates (~$10–15/person).
meals.lunch: All-you-can-eat Gateway Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — included with the Ambassador package (~$20–30 add-on or included depending on ticket tier). Features Hawaiian and Polynesian dishes.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center's Ali'i Luau (if booked) or the on-site restaurant before the evening show. Alternatively, stop at Giovanni's Shrimp Truck on the North Shore on the way back (~$15/person).

day_by_day.notes: Book Polynesian Cultural Center tickets online in advance at polynesia.com. The Ambassador Package (~$120–140/adult, ~$90–110/child) includes the buffet, all activities, and the evening show — best value for families. The center is closed on Sundays — VERIFY operating days when booking. Plan for a full 8–10 hour day.

day_by_day.morning: Kaanapali Beach Family Day — fly or take a ferry to Maui (or if staying on Oahu, visit Lanikai Beach or Ko Olina Lagoons as an alternative). If on Maui, arrive at Kaanapali Beach early to claim a spot on this iconic 3-mile stretch of golden sand. Swim, snorkel, and play in the gentle surf.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kaanapali's Whaler's Village outdoor mall for shopping and a break from the sun. Rent snorkel gear from a beachside vendor and explore the reef near Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) — a famous snorkeling spot teeming with sea turtles and tropical fish.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the traditional cliff diving ceremony at Black Rock at sunset — a free, spectacular daily event where a torch lighter dives from the lava rock into the ocean. Stroll along the Kaanapali Beachfront Walk for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your accommodation or a local café near the beach — try Gazebo Restaurant in Napili (arrive early, expect a wait) for famous macadamia nut pancakes (~$12–18/person).
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Leilani's on the Beach at Whaler's Village — fresh fish tacos, burgers, and tropical drinks with ocean views (~$18–28/person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hula Grill Kaanapali — open-air beachfront dining with Hawaiian regional cuisine and live music (~$25–40/person). Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: If flying to Maui, book inter-island flights with Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest well in advance (~$60–120/person round trip). Alternatively, this day can be spent at Ko Olina Lagoons on Oahu's west side — four calm, family-friendly man-made lagoons perfect for swimming with young children (free entry, paid parking ~$5).

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii — take a sunrise walk along Waikiki Beach for a peaceful farewell to the islands. Visit the Honolulu Farmers Market at KCC (Kapiolani Community College) if it falls on a Saturday/Tuesday — browse local produce, flowers, and artisan foods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping along Kalakaua Avenue or at Ala Moana Center (the largest open-air shopping mall in the US). Pick up macadamia nuts, Kona coffee, Hawaiian quilts, and local treats to bring home. Head to the airport for your return flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Daniel K. Inouye International Airport (HNL). Reflect on an incredible 10-day balanced family adventure spanning Southern California and the Hawaiian Islands.

meals.breakfast: Final Hawaiian breakfast at Eggs 'n Things on Saratoga Road — famous for their pancakes with whipped cream and local fruit (~$12–18/person). Expect a short wait.
meals.lunch: Last plate lunch at Ono Seafood or Ono Hawaiian Foods in Kapahulu — a true local farewell meal with poke, lomi salmon, and haupia (~$12–16/person).
meals.dinner: Airport dining at HNL or on the plane — grab a final shave ice from Island Snow or Matsumoto's before heading through security as a sweet send-off (~$4–6/person).

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at HNL at least 2.5–3 hours before your departure flight. Agricultural inspection is required when leaving Hawaii — do not attempt to bring certain fruits, plants, or fresh foods back to the mainland. Confirm all baggage weight limits. Take a final family photo at the beach before checking out!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters ideal for beginner snorkelers. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit
experiences.description: Spend a full day immersing the family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures including Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Tahitian, and Maori. Enjoy live demonstrations, canoe rides, traditional crafts, and an incredible evening luau with fire knife dancing and an all-you-can-eat buffet. One of the most educational and entertaining family experiences on the islands.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a leisurely day on one of America's most celebrated beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand on Maui's west coast. Families can swim in calm turquoise waters, build sandcastles, rent boogie boards, and watch cliff divers leap from Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) at sunset. Beachside restaurants and shave ice stands make it a perfect all-day outing.

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. The park's visitor center offers ranger-led programs designed specifically for children, making it both thrilling and educational.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

experiences.name: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food by visiting iconic local spots serving plate lunches featuring kalua pork, lomi salmon, poi, macaroni salad, and fresh poke bowls. Stop at legendary local institutions like Helena's Hawaiian Food and grab shave ice from Matsumoto's for dessert. A delicious and affordable way to connect the whole family with Hawaii's unique culinary heritage.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 11:20 AM — Flight Alaska lands. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange private luxury transfer to hotel. Check in early if possible at SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into the hotel and take a leisurely stroll around the Buena Park area. Visit a nearby spa or hotel pool to decompress after the flight. Pick up any last-minute travel essentials at a local shopping center.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at a premium local restaurant near Buena Park to celebrate the start of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Light snack or meal on the flight before landing
meals.lunch: In-flight meal or a quick premium bite at the airport upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Ranch Restaurant & Saloon (Anaheim) or a comparable upscale steakhouse near Buena Park — enjoy a hearty welcome meal

day_by_day.notes: No activities scheduled before 11:20 AM arrival. Focus Day 1 on rest and recovery. Confirm all Hawaii inter-island bookings and activity reservations this evening. Note: The hotel is in Buena Park, CA — Hawaii activities begin once you fly to the islands. Coordinate Hawaii-bound flights for Day 2 morning.

day_by_day.morning: Early checkout and private luxury transfer to LAX or John Wayne Airport for your flight to Honolulu, Oahu. Upon landing, check in to your luxury Waikiki resort (e.g., The Royal Hawaiian or Halekulani Hotel). Enjoy a welcome amenity and ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach for a gentle first afternoon in Hawaii. Rent premium beach chairs and umbrellas, take a beginner surf lesson with a private instructor, or simply wade in the warm Pacific waters with the family.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the hotel's oceanfront bar followed by a fine dining dinner with panoramic ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Grab-and-go premium breakfast at the Buena Park hotel or airport lounge before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at the resort upon arrival — try the poolside menu at The Royal Hawaiian's Mai Tai Bar
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Mer at Halekulani — Hawaii's most celebrated fine dining restaurant featuring French-Hawaiian cuisine with ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Book early morning flights to maximize time in Honolulu. Pre-arrange luxury resort check-in to avoid wait times. Confirm private airport transfer in Honolulu. Weather note: August averages 16.8°C highs with some rain — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — Depart early (7:00 AM recommended) to beat crowds at this protected marine sanctuary. Book a private guided snorkeling tour for the family with premium equipment provided. Explore the vibrant coral reef teeming with tropical fish, sea turtles, and colorful marine life in crystal-clear waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Waikiki and enjoy a leisurely afternoon at the resort pool or beach. Optional: Book a private catamaran sailing cruise along the Oahu coastline for stunning views of Diamond Head.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Hawaiian luau — book the premium Paradise Cove Luau or Germaine's Luau for an authentic cultural experience with fire dancing, hula performances, and a feast.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast buffet before departing for Hanauma Bay — try the Surf Lanai at The Royal Hawaiian
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a premium Waikiki restaurant such as Duke's Waikiki — enjoy fresh fish tacos and tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: Full luau feast at Paradise Cove — traditional kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, haupia dessert, and unlimited tropical drinks included

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations — book online at least 2 days ahead. Entry is limited to protect the ecosystem. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only. Bring underwater cameras or rent GoPros for snorkeling. Luau typically runs 5:00–9:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit — Depart by 9:00 AM for the 35-mile drive to Laie on Oahu's North Shore. Spend the morning exploring six authentic Polynesian village exhibits representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa (New Zealand), Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Participate in hands-on cultural activities like coconut husking, fire making, and traditional weaving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue at the Polynesian Cultural Center — watch the spectacular canoe pageant on the lagoon, enjoy cultural performances, and explore the IMAX theater. Upgrade to the Ali'i Luau package for a premium VIP experience with reserved seating.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the breathtaking 'HA: Breath of Life' evening show — a world-class theatrical production celebrating Polynesian culture with stunning costumes, acrobatics, and fire performances.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Gateway Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a wide spread of Pacific Island cuisine including Hawaiian, Samoan, and Tongan dishes
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau premium dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center — traditional imu-roasted kalua pig, fresh seafood, and tropical desserts with VIP seating

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ambassador VIP package for the best experience — includes guided tours, priority seating, and exclusive access. The full day runs approximately 12:00–9:30 PM. Drive or arrange a private luxury shuttle. Great for families with children of all ages.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour — Join a premium guided food tour of Honolulu's most iconic local eateries. Visit legendary spots like Rainbow Drive-In, Zippy's, and Helena's Hawaiian Food. Sample classic plate lunches featuring two scoops of rice, macaroni salad, kalua pig, lau lau, chicken katsu, and fresh poke.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chinatown Honolulu and the historic downtown area. Visit the Iolani Palace (the only royal palace on U.S. soil), browse the Honolulu Museum of Art, and stroll through the vibrant Chinatown markets. Optional: Book a private historical walking tour.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset hike or drive to Diamond Head State Monument for panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean at dusk, followed by a premium dinner back in Waikiki.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort — fresh tropical fruit, acai bowls, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Multiple tastings throughout the plate lunch food tour — a true feast of authentic Hawaiian comfort food
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nobu Honolulu — world-renowned Japanese-Peruvian fusion cuisine with premium sashimi, black cod miso, and signature cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Book the food tour with a reputable local guide company for the best insider experience. Diamond Head hike is approximately 1.6 miles round trip — wear comfortable shoes. Sunset at Diamond Head is spectacular but arrive 1 hour before sunset for parking.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Honolulu (HNL) to Kahului, Maui (OGG) — book a short 30-minute inter-island flight. Check in to your luxury Maui resort (e.g., Four Seasons Resort Maui at Wailea or Andaz Maui at Wailea). Enjoy the resort's world-class amenities and stunning ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kaanapali Beach Family Day — Drive 45 minutes north to the legendary Kaanapali Beach. Spend the afternoon on this stunning 3-mile stretch of golden sand. Rent premium beach equipment, try stand-up paddleboarding, snorkel the famous Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a), or simply relax under a private cabana.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the traditional cliff diving ceremony at Black Rock at sunset — a Maui tradition performed nightly. Enjoy dinner at a beachfront restaurant in Kaanapali.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Honolulu resort or airport lounge before the inter-island flight
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Leilani's on the Beach at Kaanapali — fresh fish, burgers, and tropical cocktails with ocean views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Japengo at the Hyatt Regency Maui — premium Pacific Rim cuisine with fresh sushi, seafood, and stunning sunset views over Kaanapali Beach

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights on Hawaiian Airlines for the best service. Kaanapali Beach is consistently ranked among America's best beaches. The Black Rock cliff diving ceremony occurs nightly at sunset — arrive 30 minutes early for a good viewing spot. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Private Road to Hana luxury tour — Hire a private driver and luxury vehicle for the iconic Road to Hana experience. Stop at Twin Falls for a refreshing swim, explore the lush Waikamoi Nature Trail, and marvel at the dramatic Wailua Falls. Enjoy exclusive stops away from the crowds with a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana journey — visit the black sand beach at Wai'anapanapa State Park (book entry in advance), explore the Seven Sacred Pools at Ohe'o Gulch in Haleakala National Park, and take in the breathtaking coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort in Wailea for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a couples or family spa treatment at the resort's luxury spa, followed by a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — fuel up for the long day ahead
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the resort or stop at Coconut Glen's in Hana for legendary organic coconut ice cream and local snacks
meals.dinner: Dinner at Spago Maui at Four Seasons Wailea — Wolfgang Puck's signature California-Hawaiian cuisine with fresh local ingredients and ocean views

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is approximately 64 miles with 620 curves and 59 bridges — a private driver is strongly recommended for a premium experience. Book Wai'anapanapa State Park entry online in advance (required). Start early (7:00 AM) to avoid traffic. Bring motion sickness medication if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Haleakala Sunrise Experience — Wake at 2:30 AM for a private luxury sunrise tour to the summit of Haleakala volcano (10,023 feet). Watch the spectacular sunrise above the clouds — one of the most awe-inspiring natural experiences in Hawaii. Bring warm layers as summit temperatures can drop to near freezing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by mid-morning and rest. After lunch, enjoy a premium whale watching or dolphin watching cruise (August may offer spinner dolphin sightings). Alternatively, book a private helicopter tour of Maui's dramatic coastline, waterfalls, and volcanic landscapes.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Maui dinner at one of the island's finest restaurants, celebrating the family's incredible experiences.

meals.breakfast: Light snacks and hot beverages provided during the Haleakala sunrise tour — enjoy a full resort breakfast upon return
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch at the resort — fresh salads, grilled fish, and tropical smoothies
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mama's Fish House in Paia — Hawaii's most celebrated seafood restaurant, featuring the freshest locally caught fish with the fisherman's name on the menu. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Haleakala sunrise requires advance reservations through recreation.gov — book as early as possible as spots sell out months ahead. Dress in warm layers (temperatures near 0°C at summit). Mama's Fish House reservations should be made weeks in advance — one of Hawaii's most sought-after dining experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Maui (OGG) to Kona or Hilo, Big Island (KOA/ITO). Check in to your luxury Big Island resort (e.g., Four Seasons Resort Hualalai or Fairmont Orchid). Enjoy a brief resort orientation and morning swim in the resort's lava rock pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration — Drive to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park (approximately 1–2 hours from Kona or 45 minutes from Hilo). Witness the raw power of Kilauea, one of the world's most active volcanoes. Walk the Kilauea Iki Trail through a hardened lava lake, explore the Thurston Lava Tube, and view the glowing lava lake from the Jaggar Museum overlook.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxing evening. If lava is flowing to the ocean, arrange a premium lava boat tour or helicopter tour for a once-in-a-lifetime nighttime lava viewing experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Maui resort or airport lounge before the inter-island flight
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Rim Restaurant inside Hawaii Volcanoes National Park — enjoy panoramic views of the Kilauea caldera while dining
meals.dinner: Dinner at Beach Tree at Four Seasons Hualalai — elegant open-air dining featuring fresh Hawaiian seafood, wood-fired pizzas, and tropical cocktails on the oceanfront

day_by_day.notes: Check volcanic activity status before visiting — visit the USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory website for current conditions. Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes for lava field walking. Bring a light jacket as the park sits at 4,000 feet elevation. Lava boat and helicopter tours must be booked in advance and are weather/activity dependent.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the Big Island — Enjoy a premium snorkeling experience at Kealakekua Bay, one of Hawaii's best snorkeling spots with abundant marine life and the Captain Cook Monument. Book a private kayak and snorkel tour for an exclusive experience. Alternatively, visit the stunning green sand beach (Papakolea) or black sand beach (Punalu'u) for a unique farewell to Hawaii.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a final lunch and leisurely afternoon. Pack, check out, and arrange a private luxury transfer to Kona International Airport (KOA) for your return flight. Browse the airport's local shops for premium Hawaiian souvenirs — Kona coffee, macadamia nut chocolates, and Hawaiian sea salt.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Kona International Airport for your return flight to the mainland. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day Hawaiian adventure filled with world-class beaches, cultural immersion, volcanic wonders, and unforgettable family memories.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — indulge in a full Hawaiian breakfast spread with fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, Kona coffee, and fresh-squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Huggos on the Rocks in Kailua-Kona — casual yet premium oceanfront dining with fresh fish, lobster, and tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal — pick up premium local snacks and treats for the journey home

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Kona Airport at least 2 hours before departure. Confirm all return flight details and arrange baggage handling for any purchased souvenirs. Consider shipping large purchases home via FedEx or UPS from the resort. Kona coffee is best purchased directly from local farms — ask the concierge for recommendations. Mahalo for an incredible Hawaiian journey!
